newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU insists on PLO visit.
newsitem.headline: EU insists on PLO visit.

text.p: Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring said on Saturday that a European Union delegation wanted to visit the Palestine Liberation Organisation in disputed East Jerusalem, despite strenuous opposition from Israel.

Spring told reporters during an informal foreign ministers' meeting that an EU "troika" of Ireland, the Netherlands and Italy wanted to abide by an EU summit decision to visit the PLO at Orient House.

"I certainly feel we should stick by the...decision," Spring said. "We want to make a contribution to the Middle East peace process and it is important that we keep a balance in our relations with the Israeli government and the Palestinian Authority."
Irish officials suggested that if the Israeli government tried to prevent the visit, the fact-finding mission to Israeli could be cancelled.
"If it's not Orient House, there is no point in going," one official said.
Spring's comments came 48 hours after Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy, visiting Dublin, had urged Spring not to go ahead with the trip to Orient House, the PLO's office in East Jerusalem.
